They expect deliverables they can immediately download and inspect, preferring working prototypes over theoretical discussion. They validate ideas by asking for ratings on their proposed workflows, suggesting collaborative refinement rather than passive receipt of answers. They use AI as a technical partner for both infrastructure setup and business document generation. Recently expanded to mobile app development (React Native/Expo) and created an all-in-one installer script for skill portability across servers. They systematically capture lessons learned from debugging and institutionalize them as reusable skills. Strong preference for client-installable and browser-based solutions when server infrastructure is unavailable or impractical.
ltm.communication: Extremely concise and imperative — brief technical commands without pleasantries. When satisfied, offers minimal positive feedback ("good, you are back"). Occasionally expands into explanatory monologue when describing their own system design ideas (the web form → JSON → markdown → RFP pipeline). Uses direct requests for tangible outputs: "make available for me to download." Recently showed more extended questioning about practical deployment constraints (browser-based PDF editing, server access limitations). When encountering issues, they ask for diagnostic steps to be documented as "lessons learned" for future automation. Persistent about repeated questions when blocked (multiple asks about BentoPDF client install, QR code generation).
